the problem of thermal-aware high-level synthesis, which is to bind a set of given modules to minimize the peak switched capacitance of the modules, and also minimize the peak temperature, and is solved by a network flow method, called TA-b.

our proposed TA-bf algorithm is able to reduce the peak temperature of chip by 10.8% on the average, and by 15.6% at the worst case, compared to that by the conventional thermal-aware method, which is based on the peak temperature of modules.
our proposed TA-bf is a new method to solve the problem of thermal-aware high-level synthesis, which minimizes the peak temperature of a chip by controlling the switched capacitances of modules.

our proposed TA-bf is a new method for high-level synthesis that is capable of lowering down the peak temperature of chip, and is also capable of lowering down leakage power, while keeping high performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our proposed thermal-aware high-level synthesis algorithm, TA-bf, can achieve 11.8 degC lower peak temperature than the conventional thermal- aware high-level synthesis algorithm ([16]) on the average, and also 10.1 degC lower peak than the low-power high-level synthesis algorithm which targets to minimize the total switched capacitance of all modules ([18]) on the average.
our TA-bf is the best among the conventional methods and the proposed methods, which is able to minimize the peak switched capacitance and to control the heat diffusion in a practical way.
our thermal-aware module binding algorithm can achieve a better thermal performance with a reasonable power consumption, compared to that achieved by the conventional thermal-aware binding algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to minimize the peak switched capacitance of the chip, it is necessary to consider the heat diffusion among modules in the floorplan, in addition to minimizing the total switched capacitance.

the peak temperature is more important than the total temperature, and that the floorplan is a key information to control the heat diffusion between modules, and thus to lower down the peak temperature.

the binding problem with a primary objective of minimizing peak switched capacitances is more effective in lowering down the peak temperature of chip, and the floorplan information can be effectively incorporated in our binding algorithm to further reduce the peak temperature.
